newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads narrow modestly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads narrow modestly.

text.p: Prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities were lower in late afternoon trade on Friday, but spreads to Treasuries tightened slightly.
Pass-through prices sagged with Treasuries earlier in the day, following a stronger-than-expected core Producer Price Index (PPI) number for March.
Analysts said the selloff occurred because the data upped the odds for further interest rate hikes.
"People are going to have to assume the (Federal Reserve) is going to have to tighten again," said Astrid Adolfson, first vice president and an economist at MCM MoneyWatch Inc.
Nevertheless, mortgage traders said yield spreads narrowed amid the Treasury selloff.

"Mortgage spreads are tight," said one trader in New York. "Mortgages have done very well. If you look across the board, callable agency spreads are tight, pass-through spreads are tight ... that is probably the trend," he said.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was off 10/32 at 100-14/32 bid, yielding 114 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 8/32 at 100-16/32 bid, while Freddie Mac paper was down 9/32 at 100-22/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was down 10/32 at 99-02/32 bid to yield 6.85 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was off 15/32 at 94-28/32, yielding 6.98 percent.

Producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March compared to a 0.4 percent drop in February. But the core component, which excludes volatile food and energy components, rose 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month.
Wall Street experts had expected an unchanged reading for overall producer prices and a 0.1 percent rise in the core.
